invariants: Skills, commands, and rules may cite only repository paths, Make targets, and validator IDs that exist; governance skills-check is the mechanical enforcement. Its corpus reaches beyond this component's ownership to the prose documentation under docs/, which cites the same territory and rots the same way
The validator registry of record is governance/validators.json; skill text references validators by ID and never restates commands as a second source of truth
Hooks under .claude/hooks/ are stdlib-only Python scripts, because a uv cold start would be paid on every gated tool call

skills-check proves citations, not prose: debt-sweep spot-checks one skill per sweep against the code it describes, and a template upgrade or a batch of new skills triggers a full audit (see evaluation 2026-08-10-agent-surface-audit-loop)

User-level skills (~/.claude/skills/, e.g. task-observer) are not duplicated under .claude/skills/: a skill the harness already loads from the user profile gains nothing from a repository copy except drift. A skill update that task-observer stages for a skill here is installed like any other edit to this surface - inside gov-change and gated by skills-check - never written live
components.purpose: Claude Code operating surface: the skills, commands, rules, lifecycle hooks, and permissions that steer how coding agents work in this repository

invariants: GitHub MCP read-only is enforced at three independent layers: container flags in Compose, the settings-validator allowlist frozenset, and the runtime post-probe assert. Governance cross-checks the three rather than re-declaring the policy; drift between any two is the finding
Unreachable MCP servers are skipped, not fatal: each server gets a bounded pre-flight probe and a failure removes its tools for that turn rather than failing the turn
Tool names are prefixed per server and deduplicated, so a per-user connection cannot shadow a deployment-managed server's tool
A deployment-managed server must declare an explicit allowed_tools list; startup fails on a malformed or duplicated server name
Connection URLs are stripped of query strings and userinfo before they reach any log, manifest, or governance artifact, because the catalog supports placing a token in the URL

Google Workspace tool exposure is per-turn and reversible: a deterministic router picks the products a turn needs and the rest are gated off, but load_google_toolkit re-attaches any connected product mid-run. Gating hides schemas from one request; it never removes a capability, and a router miss must cost a round-trip rather than the ability to finish the turn

The Google tool catalog serializes in a fixed canonical order — product order first, then connection name — so identical conversation state produces byte-identical tool definitions. Database row order must never reach the provider payload, because a catalog that reshuffles between requests cannot be prompt-cached even when it is small

The approval-resume request carries a narrowed catalog, never the full one: products holding pending approvals, products already used in the run, and products the conversation named explicitly. Referenced-not-yet-used is deliberately included, because a retention set built from usage alone strands the second half of a multi-product instruction
components.purpose: Build the assistant agent and its toolsets: local tools, deployment-managed and per-user MCP servers, and the direct Google REST executor

invariants: Routes call services; they never import or call repositories directly
Repositories flush and refresh; the session auto-commits in get_db_session, so a repository that commits breaks transaction boundaries its caller owns
Every ORM schema change has an Alembic revision; the revision graph stays acyclic and connected with the recorded head
Route handlers return Any and let response_model serialize, so a response is validated once rather than twice
Settings are never imported by tooling in-process: find_env_file walks parent directories for .env and main.py configures Logfire at import scope
components.purpose: The FastAPI application: HTTP and WebSocket endpoints, services, repositories, data models, migrations, background tasks, and the CLI

invariants: Ownership spans four roots — a route, a component directory, hooks, and stores — which is why it is declared here rather than as a directory annotation: no single directory contains it
This is the one browser surface that talks to the backend directly, over a WebSocket, with the access token passed as a subprotocol so it stays out of query strings and access logs
WebSocket events are untyped dicts with no schema. The compatibility check is the set difference between what the backend produces and what this component consumes
A dropped connection refreshes the access token before reconnecting; a token expiring mid-conversation must not end it
components.purpose: The chat experience: page, components, streaming hook, and client state

invariants: The browser itself runs in a separate service; this sidecar holds no browser. Their shared token must match, and the placeholder value must never reach a running stack — make preflight-mcp refuses to start the profile until it is replaced
Reachable only on the service-egress network and only under the mcp Compose profile
This is the widest-reaching tool source in the system: it can fetch arbitrary URLs. It is deliberately not enabled by default
public_interfaces: MCP over HTTP on container port 8000
components.purpose: Expose browser automation to the agent as MCP tools, driving a separate headless Chromium service

invariants: The committed codecov.yml carries no secrets. Every credential and deployment URL arrives as a CATEGORY__KEY environment variable, which the Codecov loader applies over the file; a secret in the yaml would be a secret in git

Optional under the codecov Compose profile. Its data plane (postgres, timescale, redis, minio) is confined to codecov-internal, which is an internal network with no egress; only the gateway is reachable from service-egress, and only api and worker have egress to talk to GitHub

The Codecov stack owns its own PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, Redis, and MinIO instead of borrowing the application's. Its schema, Redis usage, and object layout are upstream-defined and would collide with the application's allocations
The gateway routes to codecov-* service names through CODECOV_*_HOST variables; the upstream defaults (api, frontend, minio) would resolve to the application's own services on shared networks

Storage is addressed through the gateway (codecov.localhost:8090 in dev, codecov.<DOMAIN>:443 in prod), never at codecov-minio directly: Codecov signs that host:port into the presigned URLs it hands to uploaders and uses it for its own client, so it must be one name that resolves inside Docker and outside it. The alias lives only on codecov-internal and the gateway listens on the same port it is published on
make preflight-codecov refuses to start the profile while any secret still holds its placeholder default; a placeholder cookie secret or upload token is a well-known credential

CI uploads through codecov/codecov-action with the url input pointed at this instance and are opt-in via repository configuration; without it the upload step is skipped rather than falling back to codecov.io
public_interfaces: HTTP on the gateway container port 8090 (loopback 8090 in dev, codecov.<DOMAIN> via Traefik in prod)
components.purpose: Self-hosted Codecov: receives backend and frontend coverage reports from CI and serves the coverage UI, so coverage history is deployment-owned rather than delegated to codecov.io

invariants: Runs in remote conversion mode against the same Docling Serve instance the ingestion path uses, with a compatible timeout and retry budget. Two Docling paths that disagree about the endpoint would give the agent and the ingestion pipeline different answers about the same document
Local fallback conversion stays disabled: a silent fallback would move GPU work into a sidecar sized for none
Reachable only on the service-egress network and only under the mcp Compose profile
public_interfaces: MCP over HTTP on container port 8000
components.purpose: Expose Docling document conversion to the agent as MCP tools, in remote mode against the shared Docling Serve instance

invariants: One instance serves both Docling paths. The ingestion and chat-upload client and the MCP sidecar must resolve to the same URL with compatible timeouts; see ADR-004
Its model cache is an external preserved volume mounted read-only, so a container restart never re-downloads models and no service can corrupt the cache
Models load lazily rather than at boot, so a cold start is fast and the first conversion is slow
components.purpose: GPU-backed document conversion service shared by the ingestion path and the docling-mcp sidecar

invariants: Provider selection is configuration, not code: adding a provider means adding a module under providers/ that satisfies the base interface, never branching in the service
The default provider writes to stdout, so a development environment cannot send real mail by accident
Templates live with the domain rather than in a shared template directory, because their content is part of this component's contract
components.purpose: Render and deliver transactional email through a pluggable provider

invariants: The browser never calls the backend origin directly for REST. Every call goes page to client to proxy route handler to FastAPI route, and an API change is incomplete until the proxy handler is updated too. Impact analysis that skips the proxy hop reports the wrong blast radius
The chat WebSocket is the single documented exception: it connects to the backend directly with the access token as a subprotocol, deliberately keeping the token out of query strings and access logs
Route extraction normalizes the [locale] segment, so the English and Polish routes are one route with two translations rather than two routes
NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are build arguments baked into the image, not runtime configuration. Changing one requires a rebuild, so they can never be corrected by restarting a container
Generated frontend assets are regenerated from their source, never hand-edited
components.purpose: The Next.js application: localized pages, UI components, client state, and the proxy layer that fronts every REST call to the backend

invariants: Read-only is enforced at three independent layers: the container command flags, the settings-validator allowlist frozenset, and a runtime post-probe assert. Governance cross-checks the three; drift between any two is the finding
The tool allowlist is identical at every layer. Widening it at one layer only is the exact failure this cross-check exists to catch
Image-only: there is no directory anywhere in the repository that could hold an annotation for this component, which is why it is declared here
public_interfaces: MCP over HTTP on container port 8082
components.purpose: Read-only GitHub MCP server available to the agent under the mcp Compose profile

invariants: Spans two roots, which is why it is declared here rather than annotated in either one
The CLI never imports application code in-process; anything that must execute it runs in a scrubbed subprocess
Generated output is byte-reproducible: LF, UTF-8 without BOM, sorted keys, no timestamps. Two syncs with no source change produce no diff
Automation may regenerate derived files and propose changes, but may not weaken a policy, broaden a permission, accept a security exception, or approve its own governance change
components.purpose: The governance control plane: contract, schemas, policies, manifests, history, and the CLI that maintains them

invariants: These edges live in database rows, not in any file. Static extraction cannot enumerate them, so they are recorded only from runtime evidence with provenance database, under the runtime-evidence rules, and never statically assumed

Bearer tokens and the full connection URL are encrypted at rest: because the catalog supports placing a token in the URL, the url column keeps only the credential-stripped form (no query string, fragment, or userinfo) and only the Fernet-encrypted connect_url is ever used to open a connection. Every governance surface still strips query strings and userinfo before storing or logging a URL

Every tool from a user-added MCP server that is not annotated readOnlyHint pauses for the same deferred-tool human approval the Google write tools use. Approval is fail-closed: an unannotated tool is treated as a mutation, so allowed_tools unset widens exposure but never bypasses the gate

The stored URL is SSRF-revalidated at connection time, not only at write time: the per-turn toolset build re-runs the DNS check ahead of the probe cache, and the connection test endpoint revalidates before probing. Deployment-managed sidecar URLs are exempt because they legitimately resolve to internal addresses
components.purpose: Per-user MCP connections: the privileged tool surface that exists only as database rows

invariants: The general and RAG buckets stay distinct and are addressed with separate endpoint and credential settings, so a misconfiguration cannot silently merge user media with the RAG corpus
Addressed S3-compatibly through boto3; there is no MinIO-specific client and no MINIO_* application setting
public_interfaces: S3 API on the data-internal network
components.purpose: S3-compatible object storage for uploaded media and RAG source documents

invariants: No Compose file declares this. It runs on the host and containers reach it through the Docker-internal host alias, so without modelling it as a component the embedding and reranker dependency edges simply vanish from the graph
It must serve the contracted embedding model at 1024 dimensions; make preflight-model probes exactly that and additionally checks the reranker returns a finite score
It is a single point of failure for both ingestion and retrieval, and it is not restarted or health-managed by any Compose lifecycle target
components.purpose: Docker Model Runner on the host, serving embeddings and the reranker

invariants: Reachable only on data-internal, which is an internal network with no egress. The database is never published to a host port outside the dev stack
Vector columns are 1024-dimensional and a CHECK constraint enforces it; see ADR-002
The image is pinned by digest and must remain a pgvector build. A plain postgres image satisfies every migration up to 0026 and then fails, which is how it was caught in CI
public_interfaces: PostgreSQL wire protocol on the data-internal network
components.purpose: PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension: application tables, the vector store, and the durable embedding cache

invariants: Embedding dimension is 1024 end to end: settings EMBEDDING_DIMENSION, the vectorstore guard and DDL, the migration CHECK constraint, the persisted per-collection embedding_fingerprint, and the embedding cache key version. Drift between any two of the five is the finding, not just a mismatch against settings
Re-ingestion preserves stable document identity, so re-running a sync updates a document rather than duplicating it
The embedding cache is two-level: Redis L1 backed by a durable PostgreSQL pgvector L2 with versioned keys. Changing what the key hashes invalidates both levels and is part of the dimension contract

Ingestion and chat uploads reach Docling Serve over the direct HTTP client; the docling-mcp sidecar is an agent tool source, not this path. Both must resolve to the same DOCLING_SERVE_URL with compatible timeout and retry budgets
The general and RAG object-storage buckets stay distinct, with separate credentials and endpoints
components.purpose: Convert, chunk, embed, persist, retrieve, and rerank documents

invariants: Logical database allocations are explicit and exclusive: 0 general cache, 1 Taskiq broker, 2 Taskiq results, 3 embedding cache level one. A new consumer may not quietly reuse an allocated database
Persistence is on (appendonly with everysec fsync), and its volume is external preserved state this repository did not create
Production requires a password; the base and dev stacks deliberately run without one on an internal network
public_interfaces: Redis protocol on the data-internal network
components.purpose: Cache, Taskiq broker and result backend, and the level-one embedding cache

invariants: The only service in any stack that publishes a non-loopback host port. Its dashboard is bound to loopback
The HTTP port is configurable because this host already runs IIS on port 80; a hard-coded 80 would collide
Present only under the edge profile of the production stack
public_interfaces: HTTP and HTTPS on the host
components.purpose: Production edge: TLS termination, Let's Encrypt, and host-based routing to the API and frontend
